A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-PruMerge and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The complete documents support comparison, including v5's appendix, which largely relocates v1's limitations.

before.justification: v1 reports original image question-answering evaluations, token-sampling experiments, component ablations, and fine-tuning comparisons in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v5 retains original image experiments and adds PruMerge+ evaluations and inference-only Video-LLaVA experiments in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1 introduce PruMerge+, which supplements attention-selected tokens with spatially uniform samples. This adds a substantive token-selection component to the retained IQR selection and key-based merging procedure, although the revised pseudocode leaves its final token count inconsistent.

E1.justification: The six image benchmarks and LLaVA-1.5 training data are retained. v5 adds video question answering on MSVD-QA, MSRVT-QA as labeled in Table 3, and ActivityNet-QA, extending actual evaluation to multi-frame video inputs.

E2.justification: The image comparison methods remain unchanged. The new video comparison in Table 3 introduces FrozenBiLM, VideoChat, LLaMA-Adapter, Video-LLaMA, Video-ChatGPT, and Video-LLaVA as comparators against the proposed variants.

E3.justification: v5 introduces inference-only video evaluation using eight frames, 2048 original visual tokens, and gpt-3.5-turbo assessment with Accuracy and Score metrics. The sampling comparison also replaces common 40-token sequential controls with task-specific controls, including 35 tokens for POPE and 16 for ScienceQA, and revises spatial grids. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sampling analysis is revised from the common grid sweep in v1 Table 3 to task-specific comparisons in v5 Table 4, adding some settings and removing others. The questions examined by the component and fine-tuning ablations remain unchanged in the corresponding Tables 5–6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The IQR rule is a method component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v5 adds PruMerge+ image results and video results. Table 1 revises PruMerge's 7B/13B POPE scores from 86.3/86.2 to 76.3/78.5; corresponding ablation entries also change. Sampling results are added and removed under revised budgets. Video Table 3 reports ActivityNet-QA accuracy of 48.3 for PruMerge versus 45.3 for Video-LLaVA. Revised token-budget descriptions prevent treating all cross-version score differences as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equations 3.1–3.4, the IQR fences, and the underlying mathematical machinery are retained. The added attention-cost explanation and algorithmic sampling ratio do not constitute a substantive theoretical development; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central token-reduction claim remains, but v5 adds claims for PruMerge+'s accuracy–compression tradeoff and training-free generalization with improved video performance. The introduction also changes average image retention from 6.9% to 5.5%, although the conclusion still states 6.9%.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations for spatial supplementation preserving less-attended content and interprets video results as evidence of redundant video tokens. Section 3.5 further explains why LMM visual representations differ from ViT class-token representations. The original lossiness and larger-model validation limitations remain, with the future backbone example revised to Yi-34B.

D1.justification: v5 documents upper-fence use in practice and specifies the video evaluator version and frame/token configuration. It removes the promise to release code and checkpoints while retaining the project URL; actual resource availability is not established. The one-epoch LoRA description and V100-based efficiency-analysis details remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography is almost unchanged, apart from removing the Hendrycks–Gimpel GELU reference. Sections 2.1 and 3.5 sharpen the existing positioning against ViT token reduction, including a new assertion that previous work had not addressed LMM efficiency through visual-token counts.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and preliminaries receive extensive rewriting. Two related-work subsections are merged, dedicated method and discussion subsections are introduced, and limitations move into an appendix alongside a new societal-impacts paragraph. The acknowledgement is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 3 becomes a composite attention plot and token visualization; Figure 4 shrinks from eight panels to six and wraps into the text. The sampling table is redesigned into task-specific blocks beside the other ablation tables. Table 1 gains variant rows, and a new video table is added, substantially reorganizing the experimental displays.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful video validation and a PruMerge+ comparison addressing v1's accuracy–compression tradeoff. However, Algorithm 1 selects 2m tokens but still loops over and returns m, while the video text calls 256 tokens 25% of 2048. Revised POPE scores also contradict the retained outperformance claim. These inconsistencies affect the central efficiency argument and reproducibility, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain despite the broader evidence.
